self_inspection.with-skill-run3: the agent used capture.py with --motion-check, emulated prefers-reduced-motion, measured frame time in-page, and counted its own detail-ladder bands

grading.grader: a third Claude Opus agent in the same CLI session family - self-graded, not independent
grading.rescoring_note: re-scored three times: when item 15 was added (26 -> 28 items), when item 16 was added (28 -> 29), and on 2026-09-09 when item 17 (surface on the hero) was added with the kit quality tiers (29 -> 30). Then item 9 was re-worded on 2026-09-09 (lightness floor) and re-read on all five runs at the same 30-item scale, which moved the totals from 20/18/22/23/24 to 21/19/23/23/25. Only the current 30-item totals should be quoted; the '15 items', '29' and the pre-floor 30-item figures that earlier revisions of this file carried are superseded.
shared_conventions: n-a means the item's prescribed toggle or sweep was not run; it is never counted as a pass
hue families and saturation come from the checklist's own posterise-to-eight test on the canvas region of the overview frame

item 9 was re-read on 2026-09-09 under its new lightness floor (the 45% cap applies to pixels at HSL L >= 0.2, and to surfaces rather than sky or emissives): same frames, same crops, same posterise, nothing regenerated. All five runs pass it now; four totals moved by one each
item 4 fails for a run if it fails in any graded frame
the unexplained-opt-out rule is charged once, in the docs row, not multiplied across items
item 16 is counted on the run's own declared hero, at the closest frame available, by counting features in the frame rather than by reading the artifact's own report

item 17 (surface on the hero) is counted on the same hero close-up frame as item 16: it asks for material texture and occlusion, not modelled relief. It fails in the baseline and runs 1-3 - none ships a texture map or baked occlusion - and passes only in run 4, whose hero is a Blender-baked T3 GLB. Item 17 and the T3 tier were authored in the same week by the same author, so this is the least independent result in the set.

scale.note: item 15 (liveness) and item 16 (detail ladder) were added during this evaluation, each after a run failed it; item 17 (surface on the hero) was added on 2026-09-09 with the kit quality tiers. All five scorecards are scored on the 30-item scale; runs 1-3 and the baseline were re-scored from their existing frames, nothing was regenerated, and no earlier item's verdict changed. The /26, /28 and /29 totals are superseded.

totals_out_of_30.note: these are the post-floor item-9 totals (2026-09-09). Pre-floor they were 20/18/22/23/24; runs 2 and 3 tie now, and run 4 leads run 3 by two items rather than one.

capture.renderer: headless Chromium, SwiftShader software rasteriser - colours and frame rates are not GPU results
capture.without-skill: --ready-flag none --settle-ms 4000 --click "#chips button:nth-of-type(8)" --click "#chips button:nth-of-type(9)" --click "#reset-cam" (no viewer contract; nth-of-type(8) is the mill, (9) the beacon tower, matching the with-skill picks)
capture.uniform_pass: captures-uniform/ - all five builds captured with byte-identical flags: --ready-flag none --settle-ms 4000 --motion-check 2000 --expect-motion, SwiftShader. The only strictly comparable measurement, and the source of the liveness result and of image row 1.
capture.extra_settled_frames: pick-mill-settled.png in with-skill runs 1-3 and pick-cottage-settled.png in run 4: the hero's own pick button clicked, then a 5 s settle, to separate the focus framing from capture.py's 300 ms default settle against a ~0.9 s tween
capture.post_processing: every PNG in every run re-encoded identically: RGB, 256-colour adaptive palette, Floyd-Steinberg dither, zlib level 9, to stay under 400 KB. Capture-time and re-encoded hashes are both in each capture-log.json. One exception, left alone rather than treated differently: run 4's lane.png lands at 494 KB because it is the near-black defective frame and dither noise on a dark gradient does not compress.
capture.with-skill-run4: scored set, taken by the grader in SwiftShader: --all-views --click "#pick-cottage-hero" --click "#reset" --motion-check 2000 --expect-motion, plus a separate --settle-ms 5000 pass for pick-cottage-settled.png. The agent's own captures were --gpu and are not published; captures-gpu/ holds a grader-taken GPU set with the same views, labelled and not scored.

instrumentation.method: WebGL draw functions and requestAnimationFrame wrapped by a Playwright init script, the same method for all five builds; no project exposes renderer.info, so this counts real GL draw calls rather than reading three's counter. For run 4 the wrapper also separates drawn frames from requestAnimationFrame callbacks that returned without drawing (the 60 fps cap produces those on a fast host); run 4's fps figures are drawn frames.
instrumentation.without-skill: 1928.5 draw calls per frame over 128 frames; 41 frames in 3 s (~13.7 fps)
instrumentation.with-skill: 2 frames drawn in total, then 0 frames and 0 draw calls in every subsequent 3 s window; ~1000 draw calls in the one measurable frame
instrumentation.with-skill-run2: 687.4 draw calls per frame; 34 frames in 3 s (~11.3 fps)
instrumentation.driven_checks: selection, reset, pause/resume, canvas picking, orbit response, page overflow and prefers-reduced-motion were driven with Playwright on every build rather than read from the source
instrumentation.with-skill-run3: 4773.0 draw calls per frame; 15 frames in 3 s (~5.0 fps) - the highest cost of the four runs
instrumentation.with-skill-run4: 7242.0 draw calls and ~882,000 triangles per drawn frame; 7 drawn frames in 3 s (~2.3 fps), median 450 ms, SwiftShader - the highest cost of the five runs. On the unscored GPU set: 7485.2 draw calls, ~894,000 triangles, 139 drawn frames in 3 s (~46.3 fps), median 24.7 ms. The artifact measured none of this and its design system asserts 60 fps.

liveness.with-skill-run4: exit 0, differs: true (eeba3a8a... -> 6233c8ab...) in the uniform SwiftShader pass

attribution.liveness: attributable to the scaffold fix by code inspection, not by statistics: run 2 carries the clamped first-frame dt (main.js:66) and passes invalidate into createCameraRig (main.js:49-50, rigs/camera-orbit-follow.js:16,27,29), while its scene.js:134 still holds the same `if (dt <= 0) return false;` that parked run 1
attribution.everything_else: not attributable - palette, subject, layout, building count, draw-call count and the score difference are free variation between two independent generations at n=1 each
attribution.detail_ladder: run 3 is the only run to pass item 16, and the kit blueprints are the plausible cause - but unlike the liveness fix there is no code-level mechanism tying the pass to a specific skill change, and a different agent modelling a different subject explains it equally well at n=1
attribution.cost: draw calls rose 687 -> 4773 between runs 2 and 3 with no guidance covering it; not attributable in either direction, and unnoticed by run 3's own report

limits: n=1 per condition: four artifacts, one prompt, no repeats and no variance estimate; the one-item gap between runs 2 and 3 is not a result
self-graded: the grader is the same model family that generated all four artifacts
software renderer: SwiftShader colour and speed are not what a GPU would produce

the scale changed three times, each time after a run failed the new item or alongside the feature that passes it; run 3's agent could read items 15 and 16 while runs 1-2's could not, and only run 4's could read item 17 - the one item it uniquely wins - so no pair is a clean A/B
the runs used different self-inspection tools, each round's including the check the previous round failed
capture symmetry is imperfect: the with-skill builds have a viewer contract and got five named views, the baseline has none; only captures-uniform/ is method-identical
toggle tests (light removal, fog, emissives, near-plane zoom) were not run for any artifact; those items are n-a, never pass

anti-slop item 9 (45% HSL saturation cap) was ill-posed for near-black bands; it was applied mechanically to all five in the first grading, then re-worded on 2026-09-09 with a L >= 0.2 lightness floor and re-read on the same frames. All five pass it now, so it separates no pair of runs; run 3 is the only run whose posterised bands all sit above the floor, and run 2 passes by having no band above the floor at all
run 4 inspected itself on a GPU and is graded on SwiftShader frames the grader took; its own fix decisions were made from frames that are not the frames scored here

three of run 4's seven named views are damaged by camera placement (lane inside a building, cottage blocked by a lantern post, square 37.5 % filled by a wall at the near plane); the run itself reports only the first two. Since 2026-09-09 capture.py measures view_quality per capture and --expect-usable exits 6: run backwards over these five runs it flags exactly those three frames (lane near-black, square and cottage flat-occluder) out of 42, catching the wall in cottage rather than the lantern post
